page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. This processor runs at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and provides 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs, operating with one thread per core. The instance features 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple tests. In CPU-focused workloads, it achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9875.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 1282.13 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 109.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, the instance processes Redis SET operations at 22.14 million operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds reach 12.72 tokens per second for text generation using a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a predictable performance profile for general-purpose and compute-intensive workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, which is suitable for architectures utilizing external block storage. This server is appropriate for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, web serving, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.

Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on network-attached storage and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 23637.6 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 23015.19. It demonstrates solid utility for database operations, achieving 8647.45 operations in Passmark database tests, and handles Redis SET operations at 22.14 million operations per second. With its dedicated core allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is well-suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale database workloads.
